risks.risk: Credit risk in near-prime and affordable housing segments
risks.note: As the Company expands into near-prime and affordable housing, it faces higher inherent credit risk. It has started taking guarantee cover under the Credit Risk Guarantee Fund Trust for Low Income Housing as an additional mitigant, but portfolio quality in these segments remains a key watchpoint.

risks.risk: Interest rate risk from diversified borrowing mix
risks.note: BHFL's borrowings span term loans, NCDs, commercial papers, and NHB refinance across various interest benchmarks and maturities. Interest rate fluctuations from internal (maturity profile, fixed/floating mix) or external (macro, regulatory, competitive) factors can impact margins and asset-liability mismatches.

Despite a healthy LCR of 152.52%, structural and dynamic liquidity gaps are monitored by ALCO. Mismatches between assets and liabilities across time buckets could strain liquidity if not managed within regulatory and Board-approved limits.

risks.risk: Operational risk including fraud and connivance
risks.note: BHFL has a dedicated risk containment unit monitoring system-based triggers and early warning signals to prevent fraud between internal/external stakeholders. As operations scale, the complexity and volume of transactions increase the potential for operational lapses.

Reliance on digital tools, cloud infrastructure, and Account Aggregator frameworks exposes BHFL to cyber-attacks, data breaches, phishing, malware, and DDoS attacks. Mitigation requires continuous investment in multi-layered security controls aligned with ISO 27001:2022 and regulatory standards.

risks.risk: Reputational risk from customer service and digital presence
risks.note: Customer escalations on CRM, social media, and regulatory channels can lead to reputational damage. BHFL has strengthened its Online Reputation Management framework, but any service failure or negative brand mentions could erode trust in a competitive lending market.

risks.risk: Market risk on surplus fund investments
risks.note: Surplus funds are invested in government securities, treasury bills, liquid funds, and bank deposits. While these are liquid instruments, they remain subject to interest rate-driven price fluctuations, managed through modified duration and PV01 tools reviewed monthly.

one-line thesis:
The best volume quarter in the company's history sitting on top of a margin that management has now formally
guided down: *"highest ever quarterly AUM growth and quarterly disbursement in last quarter"* — disbursements
**₹19,509 crores (+33% YoY)** and AUM growth of **₹8,918 crores** against ₹5,736 crores a year ago, taking AUM to
**₹1.496 lakh crores (+24%)** — while NIM fell 14 bps to **3.7%** and FY27 guidance is for NIM to
*"moderate by 20-25 bps during FY27 from what it was in FY26."* The mechanism is explicitly **not** competitive
price-cutting but book attrition in a flat-rate world: *"whatever book is attriting, that book attrites at largely
a historical book which is at a higher yield than what the book is coming."* The quarter's other headline —
**5 bps annualized credit cost** — was disowned by management as a one-off (*"This is a one-off you can take it as
a 5 bps"*), against unchanged FY27 guidance of 10–15 bps. So the read is: a lender out-growing a 9–10% industry on
volume and operating leverage (opex/NTI 21.2% → **19.6%**), paying for it in yield, with ROE improvement
(11.6% → **12.5%**) coming from leverage rather than asset returns.

order book & pipeline:
Not an order-book business. The lender-equivalent pipeline signals given on this call:
- **Sequential disbursement momentum is accelerating:** *"grew 11% on sequential basis as against 6%
  quarter-on-quarter in Q4 FY26"* — and Q4 is seasonally the strong quarter, so the Q1 sequential gain is against
  a hard comparator.
- **Sambhav run-rate stepped up into a seasonally weaker quarter:** *"For Q1, our monthly disbursement run rate was
  close to INR450 to INR465 crores. This was INR410 to INR425 crores in Q4, which traditionally is a better for
  the industry."*
- **Attrition is the offsetting pipeline:** ~₹11,000 crores of run-off against ₹19,509 crores disbursed. Attrition is
  segment-specific — *"A developer finance, it is largely natural attrition which is a project cash flow run…
  The lease rental discounting attritions are largely led by customers selling off assets."*
- **Assignment (DA) pipeline:** ~₹2,300 crores assigned out in Q1; structurally *"12% to 13% of the book being
  assigned always"*, and DA income sits inside the guided NIM: *"the margin guidance that we have basically is at
  a total income level which also includes the DA income."*
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Home loans (54.1% of AUM, +20%)** — the growth *improved* (*"home loans growth improved to 20%"*) on
  self-help rather than competitor retreat: *"The tailwind is purely the outcome of various actions what we had
  been taking in the prime side… actions of deepening and widening there."* Product GNPA best-in-book at **34 bps**,
  down 1 bp. This is the segment carrying the BT-out exposure (§10).
- **LAP (10.3%, +22%)** — deliberately **not** affordable LAP: *"We are not in affordable LAP, we are in largely in
  a prime LAP or a high ticket LAP."* GNPA 62 bps, inside its own stated corridor — management read out seven
  quarters live: *"Q3 FY25 LAP GNPA was 0.76%, Q4 it was 0.65%, Q1 FY26 it was 0.62%, Q2 it was 0.59%, then it came
  down to 0.52% and 0.46%, it has gone back to 0.62%"*, i.e. *"a corridor of 50 bps, 60 bps, 65 bps, 70 bps."*
  Explicitly denied any Bangalore salaried-tech cohort read-across: *"There is no exception or nothing to call out
  in terms of any segment or any geography outcome."*
- **LRD (23.1%, +41%)** — the fastest-growing book and the biggest QoQ mix gainer (+70 bps). Credit profile is
  different in kind: *"in lease rental discounting you onboard a AAA customer, the general provisioning requirement
  there is very different than you onboard a local developer."*
- **Developer finance (11.4%, +19%)** — one account moved Stage 2 → Stage 3, *"where our teams are working to
  resolve that account. There is only one account."* Provisioning is judgement-led, not formula-led:
  *"In developer finance, the provisioning happens on the estimation basis the way we are seeing the account to
  move… we were aware as a management that the account is going to be in a longer-term issue."*
- **Sambhav Housing (near-prime + affordable; reported separately since last quarter)** — monthly disbursement

  *"I called out the disbursement mix only, so I had not called out the portfolio."* Affordable ATS ~**₹18 lakhs**,

6a. moat & competitive position (optiona:
- **Cost of funds is the franchise.** 7.2% and falling while peers report rising incremental costs, from three
  named, structural sources: *"one is a hedging, second is the repayment of an older higher borrowings of older
  cost… Third is reset of some of the old borrowing which were at a bit higher price which has come to lower
  price."* Supported by a diversified liability book — money market 52% / banks 38% / NHB refinance 10%, with
  *"relationship backed by 18 banks."*
- **Balance-sheet headroom is unusually large:** CAR **21.59%** on leverage of only ~**5.8×**, guided up to 6.1–6.3×.
  ROE improvement to 12.5% is being manufactured out of that headroom rather than out of asset yield.
- **Credit performance has already been monetized through the ECL model:** *"All our portfolios have been behaving
  immaculately, so there has been a downward movement in the rate applicable on most of our portfolios in the
  recalibration of the model what we did in January to March"* — an auditor-validated recalibration
  (*"validated by statutory auditors and then the external auditor"*). GNPA 29 bps / NNPA 12 bps.
- **Accounting conservatism as a differentiator:** on encashment recognition for six years, ahead of the NHB
  guidance and ahead of the peers converting this quarter — *"Whatever numbers are reported had always been
  reported even when we were unlisted company long back is always on encashment."*
- **Explicitly disclaims share-gain moat.** *"our higher growth cannot be interpreted by someone else ceding the
  space, it is we are just taking a bit more from the growth in the industry because industry is that large."*
margins & cost dynamics:
- **The compression is arithmetic, not competitive.** *"in the stable interest rate regime… whatever book is
  attriting, that book attrites at largely a historical book which is at a higher yield than what the book is
  coming. So a natural process in the stable regime is that your book what gets replaced is of a lower acquisition
  IRR than the portfolio until and unless you change the mix dramatically."*
- **Spread flat 1.7% while NIM fell 14 bps — the CFO's reconciliation:** *"spreads are basically computed basis
  portfolio yields and cost of funds. So portfolio yield as on the quarter end versus what you see as cost of funds
  as on the quarter end or for the quarter."* i.e. spread is a point-in-time construct; NIM is the period one.
- **Repricing up is off the table.** Asked directly whether bank MCLR/NHB PLR increases justify a PLR hike:
  *"we have not seen any trend for large scale acquisition pricing upward movement, which that's why which we are
  not factoring in. So that's where we say the limited opportunities."*
- **Borrowing cost pressure is acknowledged but sourced to macro, not structure:** *"banks might have increased
  MCLR and NCD borrowings in the market are priced higher specifically post — from Q4 onwards, Q4 and Q1 largely
  were in the same range. Q4 was because of a liquidity and Q1 from the macro instability due to geopolitical
  factor."*
- **Guidance is claimed to be mechanical, not conservative:** *"we are able to see every month what is going out at
  what yield and what is coming in at what yield. So that's where we are projecting doing a mathematical
  projection, we are not being either being aggressive in assumption nor being conservative in calculation."*
- **Operating leverage is capped by the NIM decline itself:** *"if you are more efficient also at the same but with
  a NIM compression means that your opex to NIM income remains looks the same while if you are even if you're more
  efficient."*
- **Assignment income will not rescue the margin:** at a constant 12–13% of AUM assigned, *"the year basis NIM
  compression is what we are calling out at a 25 bps because year basis number is not going to change."*

1. **NIM guidance is the whole equity story now.** 20–25 bps of FY27 compression with 14 bps already taken; the
   residual 6–10 bps lands in **Q2 and Q3**. Any acquisition-price weakening breaks it — management's own
   conditionality: *"assuming that the acquisition pricing in the market remains in the range where it stands."*
2. **BT-out relief is one quarter old and explicitly unconfirmed.** *"in Q1 there has been some moderation in the
   BT-out pressure on the home loan side, but we are right now cautiously watching whether it is a trend… we will
   watch for one more quarter for us to see that it is a trend which can then result into a higher AUM growth."*
   The base-rate warning is management's own: *"in last year also… the BT out rate jumped up from July onwards
   because there was a 50 bps cut in June."* **Checkable in Q2 FY27** — but undated as an event and unquantified,
   so deliberately **not** logged as a `near_term_trigger` (see §10 rule).
3. **Credit cost must roughly triple to meet guidance** (5 bps → 10–15 bps) — management already conceded the
   quarter was a one-off. Watch whether GNPA drifts to the guided 30–35 bps from 29 bps.
4. **Prime home loan is the BT-out-exposed book, and it is the largest book.** *"when we talk about a BT, we talk
   about largely the prime which is our historical book and also the segment which is most susceptible to the BT
   out by PSU or the banks."* Near-prime is protected only by youth: *"the average book will be 12 MOB… so the
   pricing acquisition there is not much of a opportunity of a BT out."*
5. **Demand is decelerating, on management's own read.** *"overall demand dynamics is slightly… muted versus what
   previously we used to see… My estimation it may not be in the range of 11%-12% what we normally assume the
   market to be there. Sales are also a bit muted."*
6. **Developer-finance concentration risk is live** — one account already in Stage 3 at 48–49% provisioning, with
   resolution *"undertaken"* and no timeline. DF is 11.4% of a ₹1.5 lakh crore book.
7. **LAP is cyclical by admission** — *"it is a customer segment which comes under a cycle there"*, corridor
   50–70 bps; Q1's 62 bps is mid-corridor, so there is room to run to 70+ without breaking the stated pattern.
8. **Macro/liability volatility** — *"volatile borrowing cost movement have been there in the money market in the
   quarter 1"*, with 52% of borrowings in money markets; *"inflation impact is yet to be assessed."*
9. **NHB thematic reviews** — management is relaxed (*"I would not call it in any way impactful to the company"*),
   but the reviews are live: *"lot of thematic audits as well, like how do you compute the PLR."*
10. **Principal-business-criteria headroom of ~146 bps** (61.46% vs 60%) constrains the non-home-loan mix that is
    the yield offset.
management quality / tone:
Precise and unusually forthcoming on bad news. Three tells of candour: the MD **volunteered** that the flattering
5 bps credit cost was a one-off before it was pressed (*"This is a one-off you can take it as a 5 bps"*); he
**refused to bank the BT-out improvement** as a trend when an easy positive was available (*"we will watch for one
more quarter"*); and he **corrected himself live** on the ₹18 crore LAP movement (*"Gaurav is correcting me… I said
INR18 crores movement, yes"*). He also declined to claim share gains that analysts were offering him
(*"our higher growth cannot be interpreted by someone else ceding the space"*) and pushed back on the
"conservatism" framing of his own margin guidance (*"we are not being either being aggressive in assumption nor
being conservative in calculation"*). Disclosure quality is good: seven quarters of LAP GNPA read out from memory,
the ECL recalibration mechanics explained end-to-end, and a new Sambhav panel plus a new AI panel added
voluntarily. Two watch-items on tone: (a) the **"ROA… 12.5% to 13%"** line in the guidance block is an
uncorrected misspeak in a prepared assessment; and (b) on regulation the answer is philosophical rather than
specific (*"we always believe regulators are there to improve the market"*, *"overbearing is probably a harsher
word"*) — no concrete read on what NHB's PLR-computation audits could cost.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **Record volumes and falling margins are the same fact.** ₹19,509 crores disbursed produced only ₹8,918 crores of
  AUM growth because ~₹11,000 crores attrited — and the attriting book is the *high-yield* book. Growth here is
  literally the mechanism of yield compression; a slower BT-out would improve **both** AUM growth and NIM, which is
  why management's refusal to bank the Q1 BT-out improvement is the single most important line on the call.
- **The provisioning "release" story is really an ECL-model story.** Analysts spent three exchanges on the ₹2,300
  crore assignment; management's own numbers show it explains only ₹13–14 crores. The real driver of flat ₹401
  crore Stage 1 provisions on +₹7,500 crores of Stage 1 assets is the **January ECL recalibration** that cut Stage 1
  rates — a permanent, auditor-blessed reset of the provisioning base, not a quarterly release.
- **Sambhav is being deliberately kept out of true affordable.** ATS ₹18 lakhs, floor at ₹10–12 lakhs, 68% salaried,
  65% bureau >750 — this is *upper* affordable / near-prime. That protects asset quality but it also means the
  yield uplift from 84:16 → 80:20 is smaller than an "affordable pivot" headline would imply.
- **LRD growing 41% is the quiet mix story.** It is now 23.1% of AUM, the biggest QoQ gainer, and it carries a
  structurally different (AAA-customer) provisioning profile — it flatters credit metrics while diluting the
  "housing finance" identity, and it is bounded by the 61.46% principal-business-criteria constraint.
- **Being early on encashment recognition is now a comparability trap.** With peers switching this quarter,
  BAJAJHFL's *unchanged* +33% disbursement growth is apples-to-oranges against peers' optically depressed prints —
  and next quarter it will be apples-to-oranges the other way as peers catch up.
- **Opex leverage is real but will not show.** Opex/NTI improved 21.2% → 19.6% yet FY27 guidance is 19–20%,
  i.e. flat-to-worse — because the denominator (net income) is being guided down. Genuine efficiency gains are
  being consumed by margin compression before they reach the reported ratio.

one-line thesis:
The best volume quarter in the company's history sitting on top of a margin that management has now formally
guided down: *"highest ever quarterly AUM growth and quarterly disbursement in last quarter"* — disbursements
**₹19,509 crores (+33% YoY)** and AUM growth of **₹8,918 crores** against ₹5,736 crores a year ago, taking AUM to
**₹1.496 lakh crores (+24%)** — while NIM fell 14 bps to **3.7%** and FY27 guidance is for NIM to
*"moderate by 20-25 bps during FY27 from what it was in FY26."* The mechanism is explicitly **not** competitive
price-cutting but book attrition in a flat-rate world: *"whatever book is attriting, that book attrites at largely
a historical book which is at a higher yield than what the book is coming."* The quarter's other headline —
**5 bps annualized credit cost** — was disowned by management as a one-off (*"This is a one-off you can take it as
a 5 bps"*), against unchanged FY27 guidance of 10–15 bps. So the read is: a lender out-growing a 9–10% industry on
volume and operating leverage (opex/NTI 21.2% → **19.6%**), paying for it in yield, with ROE improvement
(11.6% → **12.5%**) coming from leverage rather than asset returns.

  *"Around 65% of the customers in this segment also continue to have bureau score of greater than 750"*; ATS
  **₹28 lakhs**, stable. Affordable is **one-third of Sambhav disbursement** — *"It hovers between 33% to 36% odd
  mix affordable within the Sambhav"* — and management corrected an analyst who read it as an AUM mix:
  *"I called out the disbursement mix only, so I had not called out the portfolio."* Affordable ATS ~**₹18 lakhs**,
  and deliberately at the top end of affordable: *"We are generally not in the sub INR10 lakhs or a sub INR12 lakhs
  kind of a bracket… not from INR3 lakhs-INR4 lakhs-INR5 lakhs to INR15 lakhs-INR20 lakhs."*
- **No subsidiary, associate or group entity was discussed on this call.**
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Sambhav as the yield lever.** The only structural offset management offers to yield compression is mix:
  *"there will be a uptick in the yield or the pricing in because of a change of a mix, but if we remain the same
  mix, but that opportunity is limited because prime is much larger in size compared to the Sambhav housing."*
  84:16 → 80:20 by FY27 exit is the whole optionality.
- **Geo-expansion down the tiers.** *"the geo-expansion is one of the strategies in the Sambhav housing… as we
  continue to grow more towards the non-metro and the next level of location in Sambhav, a ticket size reduction
  should come from there."* 73 urban + 72 rural locations today.
- **AI across the loan lifecycle (new Panel 17 this quarter).** *"We have added this new panel in the deck to share
  an update on few AI initiatives which have been deployed by the company to improve internal controllership and
  efficiencies on one side and customer experience on the other."* Named deployments: *"voice agent for lead
  generation, credit personal discussion call intelligence, collateral assessment intelligence and geo-analytics,
  AI customer assist platform, training platform and AI interview agent for frontline hiring"*, applied across
  *"origination, underwriting and collateral assessment and then customer service as well as in our internal
  customer processes."* Claimed payoff: *"improve conversion, evidence-based underwriting, reduce collateral risk
  and provide round-the-clock self-service support."* No quantification given.
- **Fee income optionality is disbursement-linked, not a new line:** *"fee and commission income predominantly
  considers insurance incomes, foreclosure, bounce, penal… as the disbursements have increased, basis that the
  insurance incomes have increased… it is all business linked variable incomes."*
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona:
- **Cost of funds is the franchise.** 7.2% and falling while peers report rising incremental costs, from three
  named, structural sources: *"one is a hedging, second is the repayment of an older higher borrowings of older
  cost… Third is reset of some of the old borrowing which were at a bit higher price which has come to lower
  price."* Supported by a diversified liability book — money market 52% / banks 38% / NHB refinance 10%, with
  *"relationship backed by 18 banks."*
- **Balance-sheet headroom is unusually large:** CAR **21.59%** on leverage of only ~**5.8×**, guided up to 6.1–6.3×.
  ROE improvement to 12.5% is being manufactured out of that headroom rather than out of asset yield.
- **Credit performance has already been monetized through the ECL model:** *"All our portfolios have been behaving
  immaculately, so there has been a downward movement in the rate applicable on most of our portfolios in the
  recalibration of the model what we did in January to March"* — an auditor-validated recalibration
  (*"validated by statutory auditors and then the external auditor"*). GNPA 29 bps / NNPA 12 bps.
- **Accounting conservatism as a differentiator:** on encashment recognition for six years, ahead of the NHB
  guidance and ahead of the peers converting this quarter — *"Whatever numbers are reported had always been
  reported even when we were unlisted company long back is always on encashment."*
- **Explicitly disclaims share-gain moat.** *"our higher growth cannot be interpreted by someone else ceding the
  space, it is we are just taking a bit more from the growth in the industry because industry is that large."*
margins & cost dynamics:
- **The compression is arithmetic, not competitive.** *"in the stable interest rate regime… whatever book is
  attriting, that book attrites at largely a historical book which is at a higher yield than what the book is
  coming. So a natural process in the stable regime is that your book what gets replaced is of a lower acquisition
  IRR than the portfolio until and unless you change the mix dramatically."*
- **Spread flat 1.7% while NIM fell 14 bps — the CFO's reconciliation:** *"spreads are basically computed basis
  portfolio yields and cost of funds. So portfolio yield as on the quarter end versus what you see as cost of funds
  as on the quarter end or for the quarter."* i.e. spread is a point-in-time construct; NIM is the period one.
- **Repricing up is off the table.** Asked directly whether bank MCLR/NHB PLR increases justify a PLR hike:
  *"we have not seen any trend for large scale acquisition pricing upward movement, which that's why which we are
  not factoring in. So that's where we say the limited opportunities."*
- **Borrowing cost pressure is acknowledged but sourced to macro, not structure:** *"banks might have increased
  MCLR and NCD borrowings in the market are priced higher specifically post — from Q4 onwards, Q4 and Q1 largely
  were in the same range. Q4 was because of a liquidity and Q1 from the macro instability due to geopolitical
  factor."*
- **Guidance is claimed to be mechanical, not conservative:** *"we are able to see every month what is going out at
  what yield and what is coming in at what yield. So that's where we are projecting doing a mathematical
  projection, we are not being either being aggressive in assumption nor being conservative in calculation."*
- **Operating leverage is capped by the NIM decline itself:** *"if you are more efficient also at the same but with
  a NIM compression means that your opex to NIM income remains looks the same while if you are even if you're more
  efficient."*
- **Assignment income will not rescue the margin:** at a constant 12–13% of AUM assigned, *"the year basis NIM
  compression is what we are calling out at a 25 bps because year basis number is not going to change."*
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- **Footprint: 224 branches across 182 locations** — described as *"remains"*, i.e. no branch addition was called
  out for the quarter. Sambhav operates at *"73 urban locations and 72 rural locations."*
- **Expansion is geographic within Sambhav (Tier 2/Tier 3), not a branch-capex programme.** No rupee capex figure,
  no commissioning date and no branch-addition target was given anywhere on this call.
- **The AI stack is the stated investment area** (Panel 17), again with no capex quantum and no deployment
  timeline attached.
- **Slippage watch is therefore a run-rate, not a date:** the checkable commitments are the Sambhav ₹600 crores+
  monthly run-rate *"in the next 9 months"* and the 84:16 → 80:20 home-loan mix by FY27 exit.
capital allocation:
- **CAR 21.59%**, above the regulatory limit, on leverage of ~5.8× — deliberately being consumed:
  *"Leverage levels are likely to fluctuate between 5.8 to 6.3 times. We are already at close to 5.8, so we are
  likely maybe end of the year at 6.1 or so."*
- **The ROE bridge is leverage, not returns.** ROA guided **down** (2.3% actual → 2.1–2.3% FY27) while ROE is
  guided **up** (12.5% → the *"12.5% to 13%"* figure, quoted as "ROA" — see §3 misspeak flag).
- **Assignment is a standing capital-recycling policy, not opportunism:** *"we had always been… in 12% to 13% of
  the book being assigned always. In one odd quarter it can be plus minus."*
- **Liability-side allocation shifted toward markets in Q1:** NCD mix +2.6% and ICD +10 bps, funded by bank
  borrowings −2.5% and NHB refinance −20 bps.
- **No capital raise, buyback or dividend was discussed on this call.**
- **Regulatory constraint on the mix:** principal business criteria at **61.46%** vs a 60% requirement — only
  ~146 bps of headroom, which structurally caps how far LAP/LRD/DF can outgrow home loans.
risks & watch-items:
1. **NIM guidance is the whole equity story now.** 20–25 bps of FY27 compression with 14 bps already taken; the
   residual 6–10 bps lands in **Q2 and Q3**. Any acquisition-price weakening breaks it — management's own
   conditionality: *"assuming that the acquisition pricing in the market remains in the range where it stands."*
2. **BT-out relief is one quarter old and explicitly unconfirmed.** *"in Q1 there has been some moderation in the
   BT-out pressure on the home loan side, but we are right now cautiously watching whether it is a trend… we will
   watch for one more quarter for us to see that it is a trend which can then result into a higher AUM growth."*
   The base-rate warning is management's own: *"in last year also… the BT out rate jumped up from July onwards
   because there was a 50 bps cut in June."* **Checkable in Q2 FY27** — but undated as an event and unquantified,
   so deliberately **not** logged as a `near_term_trigger` (see §10 rule).
3. **Credit cost must roughly triple to meet guidance** (5 bps → 10–15 bps) — management already conceded the
   quarter was a one-off. Watch whether GNPA drifts to the guided 30–35 bps from 29 bps.
4. **Prime home loan is the BT-out-exposed book, and it is the largest book.** *"when we talk about a BT, we talk
   about largely the prime which is our historical book and also the segment which is most susceptible to the BT
   out by PSU or the banks."* Near-prime is protected only by youth: *"the average book will be 12 MOB… so the
   pricing acquisition there is not much of a opportunity of a BT out."*
5. **Demand is decelerating, on management's own read.** *"overall demand dynamics is slightly… muted versus what
   previously we used to see… My estimation it may not be in the range of 11%-12% what we normally assume the
   market to be there. Sales are also a bit muted."*
6. **Developer-finance concentration risk is live** — one account already in Stage 3 at 48–49% provisioning, with
   resolution *"undertaken"* and no timeline. DF is 11.4% of a ₹1.5 lakh crore book.
7. **LAP is cyclical by admission** — *"it is a customer segment which comes under a cycle there"*, corridor
   50–70 bps; Q1's 62 bps is mid-corridor, so there is room to run to 70+ without breaking the stated pattern.
8. **Macro/liability volatility** — *"volatile borrowing cost movement have been there in the money market in the
   quarter 1"*, with 52% of borrowings in money markets; *"inflation impact is yet to be assessed."*
9. **NHB thematic reviews** — management is relaxed (*"I would not call it in any way impactful to the company"*),
   but the reviews are live: *"lot of thematic audits as well, like how do you compute the PLR."*
10. **Principal-business-criteria headroom of ~146 bps** (61.46% vs 60%) constrains the non-home-loan mix that is
    the yield offset.
management quality / tone:
Precise and unusually forthcoming on bad news. Three tells of candour: the MD **volunteered** that the flattering
5 bps credit cost was a one-off before it was pressed (*"This is a one-off you can take it as a 5 bps"*); he
**refused to bank the BT-out improvement** as a trend when an easy positive was available (*"we will watch for one
more quarter"*); and he **corrected himself live** on the ₹18 crore LAP movement (*"Gaurav is correcting me… I said
INR18 crores movement, yes"*). He also declined to claim share gains that analysts were offering him
(*"our higher growth cannot be interpreted by someone else ceding the space"*) and pushed back on the
"conservatism" framing of his own margin guidance (*"we are not being either being aggressive in assumption nor
being conservative in calculation"*). Disclosure quality is good: seven quarters of LAP GNPA read out from memory,
the ECL recalibration mechanics explained end-to-end, and a new Sambhav panel plus a new AI panel added
voluntarily. Two watch-items on tone: (a) the **"ROA… 12.5% to 13%"** line in the guidance block is an
uncorrected misspeak in a prepared assessment; and (b) on regulation the answer is philosophical rather than
specific (*"we always believe regulators are there to improve the market"*, *"overbearing is probably a harsher
word"*) — no concrete read on what NHB's PLR-computation audits could cost.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **Record volumes and falling margins are the same fact.** ₹19,509 crores disbursed produced only ₹8,918 crores of
  AUM growth because ~₹11,000 crores attrited — and the attriting book is the *high-yield* book. Growth here is
  literally the mechanism of yield compression; a slower BT-out would improve **both** AUM growth and NIM, which is
  why management's refusal to bank the Q1 BT-out improvement is the single most important line on the call.
- **The provisioning "release" story is really an ECL-model story.** Analysts spent three exchanges on the ₹2,300
  crore assignment; management's own numbers show it explains only ₹13–14 crores. The real driver of flat ₹401
  crore Stage 1 provisions on +₹7,500 crores of Stage 1 assets is the **January ECL recalibration** that cut Stage 1
  rates — a permanent, auditor-blessed reset of the provisioning base, not a quarterly release.
- **Sambhav is being deliberately kept out of true affordable.** ATS ₹18 lakhs, floor at ₹10–12 lakhs, 68% salaried,
  65% bureau >750 — this is *upper* affordable / near-prime. That protects asset quality but it also means the
  yield uplift from 84:16 → 80:20 is smaller than an "affordable pivot" headline would imply.
- **LRD growing 41% is the quiet mix story.** It is now 23.1% of AUM, the biggest QoQ gainer, and it carries a
  structurally different (AAA-customer) provisioning profile — it flatters credit metrics while diluting the
  "housing finance" identity, and it is bounded by the 61.46% principal-business-criteria constraint.
- **Being early on encashment recognition is now a comparability trap.** With peers switching this quarter,
  BAJAJHFL's *unchanged* +33% disbursement growth is apples-to-oranges against peers' optically depressed prints —
  and next quarter it will be apples-to-oranges the other way as peers catch up.
- **Opex leverage is real but will not show.** Opex/NTI improved 21.2% → 19.6% yet FY27 guidance is 19–20%,
  i.e. flat-to-worse — because the denominator (net income) is being guided down. Genuine efficiency gains are
  being consumed by margin compression before they reach the reported ratio.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body:
Not an order-book business. The lender-equivalent pipeline signals given on this call:
- **Sequential disbursement momentum is accelerating:** *"grew 11% on sequential basis as against 6%
  quarter-on-quarter in Q4 FY26"* — and Q4 is seasonally the strong quarter, so the Q1 sequential gain is against
  a hard comparator.
- **Sambhav run-rate stepped up into a seasonally weaker quarter:** *"For Q1, our monthly disbursement run rate was
  close to INR450 to INR465 crores. This was INR410 to INR425 crores in Q4, which traditionally is a better for
  the industry."*
- **Attrition is the offsetting pipeline:** ~₹11,000 crores of run-off against ₹19,509 crores disbursed. Attrition is
  segment-specific — *"A developer finance, it is largely natural attrition which is a project cash flow run…
  The lease rental discounting attritions are largely led by customers selling off assets."*
- **Assignment (DA) pipeline:** ~₹2,300 crores assigned out in Q1; structurally *"12% to 13% of the book being
  assigned always"*, and DA income sits inside the guided NIM: *"the margin guidance that we have basically is at
  a total income level which also includes the DA income."*

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
FY27 "management assessment" (Panel 41), given with Q1 as is the company's practice:
- **AUM growth — anchored to a 9–10.5% industry:** *"home loan industry grew by 9.4% in FY26, assuming that the
  growth rate remains in the corridor of a 9% to 10% or a 10.5% for home loan industry, that is where we are
  projecting the FY27 assessment also in the range of what we did the last year."* No company-level AUM growth
  percentage was put on the table.
- **NIM: −20 to −25 bps for FY27 vs FY26** — *"The NIM is expected to moderate by 20-25 bps during FY27 from what
  it was in FY26."* Q1 already took 14 bps of it: *"In the first quarter there is a 14 bps decline, so you can say
  6 bps to 10 bps of a further decline what we can we may envisage in Q2 and Q3."* Management confirmed *"Yes"*
  to the analyst's framing of *"Less than 10-odd basis points"* of residual compression.
- **Cost of funds Q2 FY27:** *"We'll be sideways, Gaurav, for the current quarter 2 in cost of funds with a
  tendency overall to be minus… So overall Q2 cost of fund would be sideways with a downward bias."*
- **Opex to net income: 19%–20%** — *"We are estimating it to be 19% to 20%… but we will expect a bit of a
  movement in the positive side."* But not much operating leverage is promised: *"it would be sideways because
  there are two parts to the opex to NIM equation."*
- **Asset quality: GNPA 30–35 bps, credit cost 10–15 bps** — *"No deterioration seen in the credit behavior across
  our products and hence asset quality is expected to remain healthy with GNPA of 30-35 bps and credit costs of
  10-15 bps."*
- **PCR: 50%–60% on GNPA** — *"Provisioning coverage as per our normal guidance shall remain in between 50% to 60%."*
- **ROA: 2.1%–2.3%** for FY27.
- **Leverage: 5.8×–6.3×** — *"We are already at close to 5.8, so we are likely maybe end of the year at 6.1 or so."*
- **⚠️ Apparent misspeak, quoted verbatim, NOT corrected here:** *"So accordingly, ROA is expected to be in the
  range of between 12.5% to 13% for FY27."* Said immediately after the ROA 2.1–2.3% and leverage 5.8–6.3× lines,
  in a sentence beginning *"So accordingly"* — reads as **ROE 12.5%–13%** (Q1 ROE was 12.5%). Recorded as stated;
  verify against the deck/next quarter rather than assuming the correction.
- **Home-loan mix shift: 84:16 prime:Sambhav → 80:20 by FY27 exit** — *"today we are 84:16 in our mix within home
  loan of a prime to Sambhav. By the time we exit the year, we will be 80:20."*
- **Sambhav monthly disbursement ₹600 crores+ within 9 months** — *"business is on track to achieve our
  disbursement target of INR600 crores plus in the next 9 months, because that's what we called out during last
  quarter saying that in next 12 months our target is to cross INR600 crores, so that remains on track."*
- **Sambhav average ticket size: ₹28 lakhs → ₹26–27 lakhs by year end** — *"a downward bias of INR1 lakhs-INR2
  lakhs max as we exit the year"*; affordable ATS to stay *"INR17 lakhs-INR18 lakhs."*
- **Assignment stays 12%–13% of AUM** — *"12% to 13% of AUM is always what is assigned… at a percentage level the
  number doesn't move."*
- **BT-out assumption:** *"Slightly lower BT out rate but not very"* — i.e. only a modest improvement is baked in;
  management explicitly refuses to call it a trend yet (see §10).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Sambhav as the yield lever.** The only structural offset management offers to yield compression is mix:
  *"there will be a uptick in the yield or the pricing in because of a change of a mix, but if we remain the same
  mix, but that opportunity is limited because prime is much larger in size compared to the Sambhav housing."*
  84:16 → 80:20 by FY27 exit is the whole optionality.
- **Geo-expansion down the tiers.** *"the geo-expansion is one of the strategies in the Sambhav housing… as we
  continue to grow more towards the non-metro and the next level of location in Sambhav, a ticket size reduction
  should come from there."* 73 urban + 72 rural locations today.
- **AI across the loan lifecycle (new Panel 17 this quarter).** *"We have added this new panel in the deck to share
  an update on few AI initiatives which have been deployed by the company to improve internal controllership and
  efficiencies on one side and customer experience on the other."* Named deployments: *"voice agent for lead
  generation, credit personal discussion call intelligence, collateral assessment intelligence and geo-analytics,
  AI customer assist platform, training platform and AI interview agent for frontline hiring"*, applied across
  *"origination, underwriting and collateral assessment and then customer service as well as in our internal
  customer processes."* Claimed payoff: *"improve conversion, evidence-based underwriting, reduce collateral risk
  and provide round-the-clock self-service support."* No quantification given.
- **Fee income optionality is disbursement-linked, not a new line:** *"fee and commission income predominantly
  considers insurance incomes, foreclosure, bounce, penal… as the disbursements have increased, basis that the
  insurance incomes have increased… it is all business linked variable incomes."*

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Improving mortgage penetration in India (housing loan to GDP ratio from 8% in FY2015 to 11.23% in FY2025) and rising per capita income support structural demand for housing finance.
- Residential real estate transitioning from volume-led to value-led growth with increased demand for premium and luxury housing, while commercial real estate remains resilient with sustained investment flows and GCC leasing.
- Government structural initiatives such as 'Housing for All', PMAY 2.0, SWAMIH fund, and higher budgetary allocations for housing schemes continue to benefit the sector.
- RBI policy rate cuts (total 100 bps reduction to 5.25% in FY2026) intended to boost consumption, but also intensify margin pressure on floating-rate loans amid heightened competition from banks with lower-cost CASA funding.
- Geopolitical risks — particularly the Iran-USA-Israel conflict around Strait of Hormuz — could choke crude oil and gas supply, leading to higher costs, inflation, reduced disposable income, and dampened housing sentiment and home loan demand.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- **The compression is arithmetic, not competitive.** *"in the stable interest rate regime… whatever book is
  attriting, that book attrites at largely a historical book which is at a higher yield than what the book is
  coming. So a natural process in the stable regime is that your book what gets replaced is of a lower acquisition
  IRR than the portfolio until and unless you change the mix dramatically."*
- **Spread flat 1.7% while NIM fell 14 bps — the CFO's reconciliation:** *"spreads are basically computed basis
  portfolio yields and cost of funds. So portfolio yield as on the quarter end versus what you see as cost of funds
  as on the quarter end or for the quarter."* i.e. spread is a point-in-time construct; NIM is the period one.
- **Repricing up is off the table.** Asked directly whether bank MCLR/NHB PLR increases justify a PLR hike:
  *"we have not seen any trend for large scale acquisition pricing upward movement, which that's why which we are
  not factoring in. So that's where we say the limited opportunities."*
- **Borrowing cost pressure is acknowledged but sourced to macro, not structure:** *"banks might have increased
  MCLR and NCD borrowings in the market are priced higher specifically post — from Q4 onwards, Q4 and Q1 largely
  were in the same range. Q4 was because of a liquidity and Q1 from the macro instability due to geopolitical
  factor."*
- **Guidance is claimed to be mechanical, not conservative:** *"we are able to see every month what is going out at
  what yield and what is coming in at what yield. So that's where we are projecting doing a mathematical
  projection, we are not being either being aggressive in assumption nor being conservative in calculation."*
- **Operating leverage is capped by the NIM decline itself:** *"if you are more efficient also at the same but with
  a NIM compression means that your opex to NIM income remains looks the same while if you are even if you're more
  efficient."*
- **Assignment income will not rescue the margin:** at a constant 12–13% of AUM assigned, *"the year basis NIM
  compression is what we are calling out at a 25 bps because year basis number is not going to change."*

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- **CAR 21.59%**, above the regulatory limit, on leverage of ~5.8× — deliberately being consumed:
  *"Leverage levels are likely to fluctuate between 5.8 to 6.3 times. We are already at close to 5.8, so we are
  likely maybe end of the year at 6.1 or so."*
- **The ROE bridge is leverage, not returns.** ROA guided **down** (2.3% actual → 2.1–2.3% FY27) while ROE is
  guided **up** (12.5% → the *"12.5% to 13%"* figure, quoted as "ROA" — see §3 misspeak flag).
- **Assignment is a standing capital-recycling policy, not opportunism:** *"we had always been… in 12% to 13% of
  the book being assigned always. In one odd quarter it can be plus minus."*
- **Liability-side allocation shifted toward markets in Q1:** NCD mix +2.6% and ICD +10 bps, funded by bank
  borrowings −2.5% and NHB refinance −20 bps.
- **No capital raise, buyback or dividend was discussed on this call.**
- **Regulatory constraint on the mix:** principal business criteria at **61.46%** vs a 60% requirement — only
  ~146 bps of headroom, which structurally caps how far LAP/LRD/DF can outgrow home loans.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The annual report does not describe any specific capacity expansion, greenfield/brownfield project, or commissioning timeline for physical infrastructure. The Company's growth is balance-sheet driven through organic AUM build-up across its mortgage product suite rather than through discrete capex projects. No plant, line, or facility expansion is mentioned.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body:
Precise and unusually forthcoming on bad news. Three tells of candour: the MD **volunteered** that the flattering
5 bps credit cost was a one-off before it was pressed (*"This is a one-off you can take it as a 5 bps"*); he
**refused to bank the BT-out improvement** as a trend when an easy positive was available (*"we will watch for one
more quarter"*); and he **corrected himself live** on the ₹18 crore LAP movement (*"Gaurav is correcting me… I said
INR18 crores movement, yes"*). He also declined to claim share gains that analysts were offering him
(*"our higher growth cannot be interpreted by someone else ceding the space"*) and pushed back on the
"conservatism" framing of his own margin guidance (*"we are not being either being aggressive in assumption nor
being conservative in calculation"*). Disclosure quality is good: seven quarters of LAP GNPA read out from memory,
the ECL recalibration mechanics explained end-to-end, and a new Sambhav panel plus a new AI panel added
voluntarily. Two watch-items on tone: (a) the **"ROA… 12.5% to 13%"** line in the guidance block is an
uncorrected misspeak in a prepared assessment; and (b) on regulation the answer is philosophical rather than
specific (*"we always believe regulators are there to improve the market"*, *"overbearing is probably a harsher
word"*) — no concrete read on what NHB's PLR-computation audits could cost.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Scale and low-risk anchor products: prime home loans and LRD deliver volume with low credit risk, evidenced by Gross NPA of 0.27% and Net NPA of 0.11%.
- Diversified funding and strong credit profile: AAA/A1+ ratings enable diversified borrowing mix (bank loans, NCDs, CP) and cost optimization; CRAR of 22.46%.
- Omnichannel sourcing and micro-market execution: direct (developer ecosystem, digital) and indirect (channel partners, DSAs) model with location-level micro-market focus drives market share.
- Full mortgage product suite with dedicated vertical structure: separate front-end and enabling teams for prime, near-prime/affordable, and commercial segments enhance underwriting and asset quality.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
1. **NIM guidance is the whole equity story now.** 20–25 bps of FY27 compression with 14 bps already taken; the
   residual 6–10 bps lands in **Q2 and Q3**. Any acquisition-price weakening breaks it — management's own
   conditionality: *"assuming that the acquisition pricing in the market remains in the range where it stands."*
2. **BT-out relief is one quarter old and explicitly unconfirmed.** *"in Q1 there has been some moderation in the
   BT-out pressure on the home loan side, but we are right now cautiously watching whether it is a trend… we will
   watch for one more quarter for us to see that it is a trend which can then result into a higher AUM growth."*
   The base-rate warning is management's own: *"in last year also… the BT out rate jumped up from July onwards
   because there was a 50 bps cut in June."* **Checkable in Q2 FY27** — but undated as an event and unquantified,
   so deliberately **not** logged as a `near_term_trigger` (see §10 rule).
3. **Credit cost must roughly triple to meet guidance** (5 bps → 10–15 bps) — management already conceded the
   quarter was a one-off. Watch whether GNPA drifts to the guided 30–35 bps from 29 bps.
4. **Prime home loan is the BT-out-exposed book, and it is the largest book.** *"when we talk about a BT, we talk
   about largely the prime which is our historical book and also the segment which is most susceptible to the BT
   out by PSU or the banks."* Near-prime is protected only by youth: *"the average book will be 12 MOB… so the
   pricing acquisition there is not much of a opportunity of a BT out."*
5. **Demand is decelerating, on management's own read.** *"overall demand dynamics is slightly… muted versus what
   previously we used to see… My estimation it may not be in the range of 11%-12% what we normally assume the
   market to be there. Sales are also a bit muted."*
6. **Developer-finance concentration risk is live** — one account already in Stage 3 at 48–49% provisioning, with
   resolution *"undertaken"* and no timeline. DF is 11.4% of a ₹1.5 lakh crore book.
7. **LAP is cyclical by admission** — *"it is a customer segment which comes under a cycle there"*, corridor
   50–70 bps; Q1's 62 bps is mid-corridor, so there is room to run to 70+ without breaking the stated pattern.
8. **Macro/liability volatility** — *"volatile borrowing cost movement have been there in the money market in the
   quarter 1"*, with 52% of borrowings in money markets; *"inflation impact is yet to be assessed."*
9. **NHB thematic reviews** — management is relaxed (*"I would not call it in any way impactful to the company"*),
   but the reviews are live: *"lot of thematic audits as well, like how do you compute the PLR."*
10. **Principal-business-criteria headroom of ~146 bps** (61.46% vs 60%) constrains the non-home-loan mix that is
    the yield offset.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- **Record volumes and falling margins are the same fact.** ₹19,509 crores disbursed produced only ₹8,918 crores of
  AUM growth because ~₹11,000 crores attrited — and the attriting book is the *high-yield* book. Growth here is
  literally the mechanism of yield compression; a slower BT-out would improve **both** AUM growth and NIM, which is
  why management's refusal to bank the Q1 BT-out improvement is the single most important line on the call.
- **The provisioning "release" story is really an ECL-model story.** Analysts spent three exchanges on the ₹2,300
  crore assignment; management's own numbers show it explains only ₹13–14 crores. The real driver of flat ₹401
  crore Stage 1 provisions on +₹7,500 crores of Stage 1 assets is the **January ECL recalibration** that cut Stage 1
  rates — a permanent, auditor-blessed reset of the provisioning base, not a quarterly release.
- **Sambhav is being deliberately kept out of true affordable.** ATS ₹18 lakhs, floor at ₹10–12 lakhs, 68% salaried,
  65% bureau >750 — this is *upper* affordable / near-prime. That protects asset quality but it also means the
  yield uplift from 84:16 → 80:20 is smaller than an "affordable pivot" headline would imply.
- **LRD growing 41% is the quiet mix story.** It is now 23.1% of AUM, the biggest QoQ gainer, and it carries a
  structurally different (AAA-customer) provisioning profile — it flatters credit metrics while diluting the
  "housing finance" identity, and it is bounded by the 61.46% principal-business-criteria constraint.
- **Being early on encashment recognition is now a comparability trap.** With peers switching this quarter,
  BAJAJHFL's *unchanged* +33% disbursement growth is apples-to-oranges against peers' optically depressed prints —
  and next quarter it will be apples-to-oranges the other way as peers catch up.
- **Opex leverage is real but will not show.** Opex/NTI improved 21.2% → 19.6% yet FY27 guidance is 19–20%,
  i.e. flat-to-worse — because the denominator (net income) is being guided down. Genuine efficiency gains are
  being consumed by margin compression before they reach the reported ratio.
